newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls, Motorola, HighwayMaster in pact.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls, Motorola, HighwayMaster in pact.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc, Motorola Inc, and HighwayMaster Communications Inc said Tuesday they will further develop AutoLink, a communications system for cars and trucks.

This technology will link vehicles to a 24-hour-per-day, national network that can provide roadside assistance, emergency response, Global Positioning System (GPS) satellite-based navigation support, theft notification, and interactive messaging and information services.
AutoLink has been in testing for a year.

The companies said they expect AutoLink to enhance significantly an automobile's appeal to consumers. AutoLink is expected to retail as an option on future vehicles for about $500, plus a monthly subscription charge.
In the future, AutoLink may also provide drivers with access to the Internet, the companies said in a statement.
AutoLink will be accessed through an overhead display developed by Prince, a subsidiary of Johnson Controls. It is expected to be available for production vehicles by the end of 1997.
Motorola will provide the GPS receiver, wireless modem and cellular phone, and will be responsible for end-to-end system operations for AutoLink customers.
Highwaymaster will provide two-way voice/data messaging in the United States and Canada.
Johnson Controls supplies automotive seating and interior systems. Prince provides automotive interior systems and electronics.
